KEY INFORMATION
Important information to know about this research study:

items: The purpose of this study is to understand whether people using a helper tool for the first time can understand how to use it to provide real-time assistance to a person using a single-user virtual reality application

If you choose to participate, you will be asked to interact with a web application designed to help a person using a virtual reality application. You will then be asked a few questions about your experience. This will take approximately 20 minutes
Risks or discomfort from this research are expected to be minimal
The study will have no direct benefits to you
You will be paid $2 for your participation
You will be provided with a copy of this consent form
Taking part in this research project is voluntary. You do not have to participate, and you can stop at any time.

blocks.text: Invitation
You are invited to take part in this research study. The information in this form is meant to help you decide whether to participate. If you have any questions, please ask.
Why are you being asked to be in this research study?
You are being asked to be in this study in order to evaluate the understandability of a helper tool. In order to participate you must at least be 18 years old.
What is the reason for doing this research study?

The purpose of this research study is to understand whether people using a helper tool for the first time can understand how to use it to provide real-time assistance to a person using a single-user virtual reality application. This study focuses on whether people can identify the appropriate part of the helper tool to use when deciding how to assist the VR user in different scenarios.
What will be done during this research study?

You will be asked to first read a brief introduction explaining the purpose of the study and your role. You will then complete a series of scenario-based questions about the helper tool. For each question, you will see the helper tool and your task is to click the part of the helper tool that best answers the question. The helper tool includes several regions, after you click a region, the selected region will be highlighted. You may change your selection before moving to the next question. Only your final selected region for each question will be recorded as your answer. You will not be told whether each answer is correct during the study.

Afterward, you will be asked to complete a short survey with questions about your experience using the helper tool as well as a few demographic questions such as age, gender, and prior VR experience. Your answers to the survey will not affect your compensation in any way. At the end of the survey, you will receive a completion code. You will copy and paste this code into Amazon Mechanical Turk to receive payment for completing the study.
What are the possible risks or discomforts of being in this research study?
There are no known risks to you from being in this research study.
What are the possible benefits to you, other people, or society?

You are not expected to get any benefit from being in this study. This research may help us understand whether people can use the helper tool in real-time to provide assistance in VR activities. The results may help improve future tools for supporting VR users who may need assistance during VR activities.
Will you be compensated for being in this research study?
You will receive $2 for participating in this study.
How will information about you be protected?
Reasonable steps will be taken to protect your privacy and the confidentiality of your study data.

This study does not collect your name, email address, or any other direct personal identifiers. The only identifying information the researchers will receive is your Amazon Mechanical Turk Worker ID, which is used solely to process your payment. In study records, you will be referred to only by a researcher-assigned ID, not your Worker ID.
The data will be stored electronically on a secure server and will only be seen by the research team during the study and for 5 years or longer after the study is complete.

The only persons who will have access to your identifiable private research records are the study personnel, the Institutional Review Board (IRB), and any other person, agency, or sponsor as required by law. The information from this study may be published in scientific journals or presented at scientific meetings but the data will be reported as group or summarized data and your identity will be kept strictly confidential.
How will information collected from you be shared and used?
Information collected from you for this study will not be shared beyond the research team listed above
Are there any potential conflicts of interest you should be aware of?
The investigators responsible for this study do not report any potential conflicts of interest related to this study.
What should you do if you have a problem during this research study?

Your welfare is the major concern of every member of the research team. If you have a problem as a direct result of being in this study, you should immediately contact one of the people listed at the beginning or end of this consent form.
What are your rights as a research subject?
You may ask any questions concerning this research and have those questions answered before agreeing to participate in the study and during the study.
For study related questions, please contact the investigators listed below.

blocks.text: What will happen if you decide not to be in this research study or decide to stop participating once you start?

You can decide not to be in this research study, or you can stop being in this research study (withdraw) at any time before, during, or after the research begins for any reason. Deciding not to be in this research study or deciding to withdraw will not affect your relationship with the investigator or with the University of Rhode Island.
You will not lose any benefits to which you are entitled.
